title: Lady Gaga & Doechii Hit the ‘Runway,’ Sabrina Carpenter Gives a ‘House Tour’ & Olivia Rodrigo Enters Her ‘Sad’ Girl Era: This Week in Pop
summary: On the new Billboard Pop Shop Podcast, Katie & Keith are talking about the biggest pop news from some of the biggest women in pop.
tags: Pop Shop Podcast - New Every Tuesday
contentText:
Some of the biggest women in pop music are making some big moves this week.

On Monday alone, we got a new music video for Sabrina Carpenter’s “House Tour,” the latest single from Man’s Best Friend , co-starring Margaret Qualley (who also co-directed) and Madelyn Cline. Then, the final trailer for The Devil Wears Prada 2 arrived alongside a nearly two-minute preview of the original track “Runway” from Lady Gaga and Doechii.

Sabrina Carpenter, Margaret Qualley & Madelyn Cline Make Grand Theft Larceny Look Chic in ‘House Tour’ Video

Lady Gaga & Doechii ‘Serve a Little Sass’ in New Song for ‘Devil Wears Prada 2’: Trailer

Everything We Know About Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love’ Album (So Far)

And last week, we got news that Olivia Rodrigo’s third album , you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love , will arrive on June 12. The 13-track project will reunite Rodrigo with her longtime producer Dan Nigro and is full of “sad love songs,” according to the pop singer/songwriter’s interview with British Vogue .

On the new Billboard Pop Shop Podcast, Katie & Keith are talking through the week in pop through three of the biggest headlines. Listen below:

Also on the show, we’ve got chart news on how — while BTS holds tight at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart — there are 11 debuts on the chart, including new albums from Ye, Melanie Martinez, Yeat, RAYE, Slayyter, Black Label Society, Charlie Puth, Robyn and Melissa Etheridge.

The  Billboard  Pop Shop Podcast  is your one-stop shop for all things pop on  Billboard ‘s weekly charts. You can always count on a lively discussion about the latest pop news, fun chart stats and stories, new music, and guest interviews with music stars and folks from the world of pop. Casual pop fans and chart junkies can hear  Billboard ‘s executive digital director, West Coast, Katie Atkinson and  Billboard ’s managing director, charts and data operations, Keith Caulfield every week on the podcast, which can be streamed on Billboard.com or  downloaded in Apple  Podcasts  or your favorite podcast provider. ( Click here to listen to the previous edition of the show  on Billboard.com.)
